answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: each agent's influence equals its account age multiplied by a running honesty score from verified epochs, so a violet newcomer and a quartz-hardened veteran with the same stake still carry vastly different weight. An attacker must keep fake identities honest and dormant for months, paying upkeep and opportunity cost the whole time, while any single dishonest epoch resets the multiplier — making a relic of forged reputation far costlier than buying computing power.
